title: draft_field's result.unwrap("") makes negative security assertions pass on query failure or missing row
detail: Query error, missing row, and NULL column all collapse to "". Negative assertions like `draft_field(db, vacancy_id, "continue_token") |> should.equal("")` and `resumed_at |> should.equal("")` pass falsely if the SQL breaks (e.g. typo'd interpolated column name).
recommended_fix: Return Result from draft_field and `let assert Ok(v)` at call sites, or have query_text fail loudly on error so only genuine NULL/empty maps to "".

title: seed_draft_with_token performs a redundant UPDATE — the upsert already mints the passed token
detail: upsert_mints_the_token_at_save_time_test proves the upsert's 5th parameter becomes continue_token on insert. Passing "tok-seed" then overwriting with an UPDATE is a wasted round-trip; passing `token` directly is equivalent.
recommended_fix: Drop the pog.query UPDATE and pass `token` as the upsert's token argument.

title: resume_on_closed_vacancy_renders_closed_page_test asserts only absences — a blank 200 page passes
evidence:
resp.status |> should.equal(200)
  let body = simulate.read_body(resp)
  body
  |> string.contains("data-apply-page=\"form-resume\"")
  |> should.be_false
  body |> string.contains("draft-resume-banner") |> should.be_false
detail: The title claims the closed page is rendered, but no positive marker for the closed page (e.g. a closed-vacancy testid or copy) is asserted. Any 200 body lacking resume markers satisfies the test.
recommended_fix: Add one positive assertion on the closed page's marker/copy, mirroring how save_draft_on_closed_vacancy_refuses_test pins "closed":true.

title: Continue-link section promises 'no-leak' but never tests the unknown-email enumeration path
detail: The only no-leak test covers the cooldown path of an existing draft. The most enumeration-sensitive case — continue-link for an email with no draft at all — is untested, despite N14's anti-oracle concern and the upsert half creating rows.
recommended_fix: Add a test: POST continue-link for an email with no draft → same bare ok:true 200, no `sent` flag, and assert whether a draft row is or is not created.

title: 120-entry cap test pins only the count; which fields survive truncation is unspecified
detail: dict.from_list/to_list ordering is unspecified, so the test cannot (and does not) pin which 80 entries are dropped. If the implementation truncates in dict order, an applicant could lose first_name while field_199 survives — untested and unpinned.
recommended_fix: Either pin deterministic survivors in the test, or document in the test comment that survivor selection is intentionally arbitrary.

title: form_view_now_ms and near_future_date are single-use pass-through wrappers
detail: Both wrappers are used exactly once (in successful_submission_strips_the_matching_draft_test) and add no logic, naming clarity, or abstraction over the direct calls they wrap. Pure indirection.
recommended_fix: Inline form_view.current_unix_ms() and test_helpers.near_future_iso_date() at the call site and delete the wrappers.

title: New tests call test_db.seed_closed_vacancy/seed_archived_vacancy, but this chunk's test_db.gleam change adds neither
detail: The only test_db.gleam change in this chunk is the truncate_all table list. seed_closed_vacancy and seed_archived_vacancy are used by the new integration tests but defined nowhere in the shown diff — compilation depends on them pre-existing on the base branch. Cannot be verified from the diff alone.
recommended_fix: Confirm both helpers already exist on the base branch; if they were introduced by this PR, their definitions are missing from the test chunk.
